facebook.post: This week on Longmont Locals, we learned a piece of city history that's hiding in plain sight all over town. When Longmont voters approved the city's first municipal power plant in 1912, the Lyons Hydroelectric Plant, the city council showed its appreciation by giving every resident a free porch light. Those funky pedestal lights you see everywhere? They're the descendants of that original tradition, installed starting in the sixties when the city transitioned from individual porch lights to street lighting. Longmont now has about 9,000 of them, and they also serve as electric meters so readers don't have to trek into backyards. Have you ever wondered what the story was behind those lights, or do you have one in front of your house?
